771: ### 8.2 Config Versioning & Schema Migration
772: 
773: Each config file includes a `configVersion` integer field. On load, the owning
774: module:
775: 1. Reads the stored version
776: 2. Performs incremental migration if the stored version is older than the current schema
777: 3. Falls back to safe defaults if migration is impossible or the file is corrupt
778: 4. Writes the updated config with the current version

797: };
798: ```

802: ### 8.4 Config Consumer Notification & Hot Reload
803: 
804: When the web portal saves any config, it calls:
805: ```cpp
806: appContext.getConfigManager().requestReload();
807: ```
808: 
809: On the next `tick()`, the framework safely executes the reload on the main thread
810: and calls `reapplyConfig()` on all registered `iConfigurable` consumers. This is
811: an EventBus-dispatched reload — **no device reboot required**.
812: 
813: ### 8.5 JSON Memory Safety
814: 
815: **`DynamicJsonDocument` is banned project-wide.** All JSON operations must use
816: `StaticJsonDocument<N>` with pre-calculated capacity sizes. `DynamicJsonDocument`
817: causes heap fragmentation and OOM crashes on ESP32's limited heap.
818: 
819: ```cpp
820: // ✅ Correct — bounded, predictable
821: StaticJsonDocument<512> doc;
822: 
823: // ❌ Banned — heap fragmented, unpredictable
824: DynamicJsonDocument doc(1024);
825: ```

1214: ### 12.6 PlatformIO LDF Constraints
1215: 
1216: > **Critical:** PlatformIO's Library Dependency Finder (LDF) scans `#include`
1217: > directives as **text patterns** regardless of `#ifdef` preprocessor guards.
1218: > A conditional `#include "Application.hpp"` inside `#ifndef NATIVE_BUILD` will
1219: > still trigger LDF to resolve and compile the entire dependency chain.
1220: 
1221: **Mitigation strategies:**
1222: - Forward-declare types in headers; include only in `.cpp` files behind guards
1223: - `library.json` files should have NO `"platforms"` or `"frameworks"` restrictions
1224:   (unless the library is genuinely platform-specific)
1225: - Never include `Application.hpp` in display module native-visible translation units
1226: - Use `lib_extra_dirs = modules` so headers resolve by basename (e.g.,

 * Description: Pure abstract interface representing a component that is ticked in the main application loop.
 *
 * Exported Functions/Classes:
 * - ITickable: Interface for periodic loop scheduling.
 *   - tick(): Main loop callback executed periodically.
 */

#ifndef I_TICKABLE_HPP
#define I_TICKABLE_HPP

#include <stdint.h>

/**
 * @brief Pure abstract interface representing a component that is ticked in the main loop.
 *        Used for periodic execution, polling, and status transitions.
 */
class ITickable {
public:
    /**
     * @brief Virtual destructor to ensure proper cleanup of derived objects.
     */
    virtual ~ITickable() = default;

    /**
     * @brief Method called on every iteration of the main application loop.
     * @param currentMillis The current system time in milliseconds since startup.
     */
    virtual void tick(uint32_t currentMillis) = 0;
};

#endif // I_TICKABLE_HPP
"

#ifndef I_CONFIGURABLE_HPP
#define I_CONFIGURABLE_HPP

// Forward declarations
struct FrameworkConfig;

/**
 * @brief Pure abstract interface for classes that consume system configuration.
 *        Allows hot-reloading configurations at runtime.
 */
class iConfigurable {
public:
    /**
     * @brief Virtual destructor to ensure proper cleanup of derived objects.
     */
    virtual ~iConfigurable() = default;

    /**
     * @brief Callback invoked when a system configuration is loaded or updated.
     * @param config The updated framework configuration structure.
     */
    virtual void reapplyConfig(const FrameworkConfig& config) = 0;
};

#endif // I_CONFIGURABLE_HPP
"

"/*
 * ESP32 App Foundation (c) 2026 CB Labs
 * Refactored by Matt McNeill 2026 CB Labs
 *
 * https://github.com/matthewmcneill/esp32-app-foundation
 *
 * This work is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International.
 * To view a copy of this license, visit https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/
 *
 * Module: include/interfaces/iDataSource.hpp
 * Description: Pure abstract interface representing a scheduled data source provider.
 *
 * Exported Functions/Classes:
 * - PriorityTier: [Enum] Duty cycle scheduling weight.
 * - UpdateStatus: [Enum] Fetch operation results.
 * - iDataSource: Interface for API data providers.
 *   - setDataManager(): Stores the central data scheduler.
 *   - updateData(): Requests a data refresh.
 *   - executeFetch(): Runs the actual network task.
 *   - getLastErrorMsg(): Returns human-readable error details.
 *   - getNextFetchTime(): Gets scheduled execution time.
 *   - getPriorityTier(): Gets priority tier for scheduling.
 *   - setNextFetchTime(): Sets manual override execution time.
 *   - testConnection(): Executes a lightweight sanity/auth check.
 *   - lockData(): Mutex lock proxy for thread safety.
 *   - unlockData(): Mutex unlock proxy for thread safety.
 *   - getAttributionString(): Gets legal provider credits.
 *   - serializeData(): Serializes current payload to ArduinoJson objects.
 */

#ifndef I_DATA_SOURCE_HPP
#define I_DATA_SOURCE_HPP

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <ArduinoJson.h>

/**
 * @brief Priority tiers for scheduling data source updates.
 *        Allows the kernel scheduler to manage resource-constrained duty cycling.
 */
enum class PriorityTier : uint8_t {

 */
enum class AppState {
    BOOTING,        ///< Core services starting, crypto load, initial configuration load.

    APP_SETUP,      ///< WiFi connected, but application is waiting for initial setup.
    RUNNING,        ///< Normal operating state with all loops active.
    WIFI_SHUTDOWN   ///< AP mode timed out after inactivity, transitioning to low-power shutdown.
};

"# Phase 2 Implementation Plan — Core Libraries

## Audit Checklist
- [x] Reviewed by `house-style-documentation` - passed
- [x] Reviewed by `architectural-refactoring` - passed
- [x] Reviewed by `embedded-systems` - passed (Resource Impact Assessment added)

> [!NOTE]
> **IP Review Findings**: All target libraries will be placed under the `lib/` directory. Portability under `NATIVE_BUILD` is achieved by isolating ESP32 hardware dependencies (Preferences, esp_random, BoardLED, HardwareSerial, WiFiClientSecure) using conditional preprocessor compilation, enabling standard output and fixed key fallbacks on host systems.

This plan details the implementation of Phase 2 of the ESP32 App Foundation framework, porting and adapting four key utility and hardware modules from the reference application.

## Goal Description
1. Create the `lib/deviceCrypto/`, `lib/logger/`, `lib/md5Utils/`, and `lib/githubClient/` directories.
2. Implement `DeviceCrypto` supporting hardware-bound encryption with a fallback 0xAA key for native simulation.
3. Implement `Logger` supporting secret redaction and macro log levels, outputting to standard output via `printf` under native builds.
4. Implement `md5Utils` using MbedTLS for checksum verification.
5. Implement `github` release metadata querying via streaming JSON parsing.
6. Enforce strict coding standard compliance (camelCase filenames, license headers, Doxygen docstrings).

## Proposed Changes

---

### Cryptography Utility
#### [NEW] [deviceCrypto.hpp](lib/deviceCrypto/deviceCrypto.hpp)
#### [NEW] [deviceCrypto.cpp](lib/deviceCrypto/deviceCrypto.cpp)
- Implements `DeviceCrypto` using MbedTLS AES-256-CBC and PKCS#7 padding.
- Under `NATIVE_BUILD`, bypasses `<Preferences.h>` and `<esp_random.h>` to avoid compilation failures on native host.
- In native mode, initializes the master `aesKey` to a fixed 32-byte array containing `0xAA` and uses standard `rand()` for the IV, allowing identical encryption/decryption validation in host test runners.

- [x] Reviewed by `house-style-documentation` - passed

   - `McpServer` (JSON-RPC tool router registry)

597: ### 7.3 `IDisplayBoard` (U8G2 Variant)
598: 
599: ```cpp
600: class IDisplayBoard {
601: public:
602:     virtual const char* getBoardName() const = 0;
603:     virtual void onActivate() = 0;
604:     virtual void onDeactivate() = 0;
605:     virtual void tick(uint32_t ms) = 0;
606:     virtual void render(U8G2& display) = 0;  // U8G2-native
607:     virtual UpdateStatus updateData() = 0;
608:     virtual bool isScrollFinished() { return true; }
609:     virtual bool isExpired() { return false; }
610:     virtual ~IDisplayBoard() = default;
611: };
612: ```
613: 
614: #### Board Expiry Semantics
615: 
616: The `isExpired()` method controls when a board auto-dismisses. The framework uses
617: an **asymmetric expiry model** — different board types have different lifecycles:
618: 
619: - **OTA Progress**: `isExpired()` returns `true` when complete AND successful.
620:   Failed OTA persists to show the error.
621: - **Error Board**: `isExpired()` returns `true` only when explicitly `dismiss()`ed.
622:   The `fatal` flag controls UI text ("System halted") but NOT expiry.
623: - **Screensaver**: `isExpired()` returns `true` when `!_active`. Starts expired
624:   by default; controlled via `activate()`/`deactivate()` lifecycle.
625: - **Transient boards** (boot splash, loading): Auto-dismiss after their purpose
626:   is fulfilled.
627: 
628: ### 7.4 Board Registration
629: 
630: ```cpp
631: // In app setup — registering a custom board with the U8G2 display module
632: u8g2Display.registerBoard(&myDeparturesBoard);
633: ```

748: ## 8. Configuration Architecture
749: 
750: ### 8.1 Separation of Concerns
751: 
752: Configuration is split across multiple JSON files on LittleFS, organised under
753: the directory convention defined in §2.7:
754: 
755: | Path | Owner | Contents |
756: |---|---|---|
757: | `/etc/config.json` | Framework kernel | FrameworkConfig (hostname, timezone, OTA, mcpReadOnly) |
758: | `/etc/apikeys.json` | Framework kernel | KeyManager encrypted credential store |
759: | `/mod/display.json` | Display module | Brightness, flip, sleep timeout |
760: | `/mod/mqtt.json` | MQTT module | Broker host, port, credentials |
761: | `/mod/ha.json` | HA module | HA API endpoint, token reference |
762: | `/mod/scheduler.json` | Scheduler module | Schedule rules |
763: | `/app/<appname>.json` | Application | App-specific settings |
764: 
765: **Ownership rules:**
766: - Framework kernel reads/writes only `etc/`
767: - Each module reads/writes only its own file under `mod/`
768: - Application code reads/writes only `app/`
769: - No component reads or writes outside its designated directory
770: 
771: ### 8.2 Config Versioning & Schema Migration
772: 
773: Each config file includes a `configVersion` integer field. On load, the owning
774: module:
775: 1. Reads the stored version
776: 2. Performs incremental migration if the stored version is older than the current schema
777: 3. Falls back to safe defaults if migration is impossible or the file is corrupt
778: 4. Writes the updated config with the current version
779: 
780: ### 8.3 App Config Extension Pattern
781: 
782: The application defines its own struct and manages serialisation:
783: 
784: ```cpp
785: struct MyAppConfig {
786:     char stationId[13];
787:     char apiKeyId[13];
788:     int refreshInterval;
789: };
790: 
791: class MyAppConfigManager {
792:     MyAppConfig config;
793: public:
794:     void load();   // reads /app/myapp.json from LittleFS
795:     bool save();   // writes /app/myapp.json to LittleFS
796:     MyAppConfig& getConfig() { return config; }
797: };
798: ```
799: 
800: The app's web portal endpoints read/write this config independently.

#ifndef I_BOARD_LAYOUT_HPP

"# Phase 5 Walkthrough — Display Subsystem, Widget Toolkit, Scheduler, and Hardware Drivers

This document details the completed implementation of Phase 5 of the ESP32 App Foundation framework. All components are written in C++14, strictly adhere to the project's house style, and include fallback mocks to guarantee portability on host native targets.

---

## 1. Architectural Layout

```mermaid
graph TD

    App --> SC[Scheduler]
    App --> LED[BoardLED]
    App --> Btn[ButtonHandler]

    DM --> |Manages state| Splash[BootSplashBoard]
    DM --> |Manages state| Prog[ProgressBoard]

1: # Embedded Web Portals
2: 
3: This reference provides the principles and constraints required when designing web interfaces, dashboards, or captive setup portals for memory-constrained embedded systems (like the ESP32).
4: 
5: ## Design & Payloads
6: 
7: 1. **Payload Targets (<100KB)**: Keep total frontend payloads minimal. Rely on Single Page Application (SPA) designs using vanilla HTML/JS/CSS rather than heavy rendering frameworks. 
8:    - **Why?** We compress (GZIP) and deploy them as `const uint8_t PROGMEM` arrays. Serving compressed assets directly from Flash memory minimizes RAM impact and avoids the latency spikes associated with `LittleFS` runtime reads.
9: 
10: 2. **Captive Portal Environments**:
11:    - **No External CDNs**: Captive setups have zero exterior internet routing. You must rely solely on serialized, on-device assets.
12:    - **DNS Redirection**: Always implement a wildcard DNS server redirecting resolving requests (`*`) to the Access Point's gateway IP. This is required to reliably trigger the native captive portal pop-ups on iOS/Android.
13: 
14: ## Architecture & Security
15: 
16: 1. **Asynchronous Execution**:
17:    - Use `ESPAsyncWebServer` (or equivalent non-blocking paradigms).
18:    - **Why?** Legacy synchronous blocking logic pauses the core network and display loops, which starves the RTOS watchdogs and causes massive (20-30s) UI hangs.

20: 2. **Resource Protection**:
21:    - **Network Pool (Sockets)**: Validate network configs (like multiple external API keys) sequentially. Parallel polling risks exhausting the ESP32's extremely limited socket pool.
22:    - **Heap Parsing**: Apply standard memory-optimization principles heavily to inbound `HTTP POST` parsing. Use bounded `ArduinoJson` buffers (`StaticJsonDocument` or capped `DynamicJsonDocument`) to prevent malicious or accidental heap exhaustion from large payloads.
23:    - **Power State**: AP Mode (Captive Portal) draws ~100-120mA continuously. Implement an inactivity timeout (e.g., 10 minutes) to automatically shut down the AP mode, reducing both the thermal/power load and the attack surface.
24:    - **Data Exposure**: Never expose credentials (Wi-Fi passwords, API keys) via plaintext `HTTP GET` routing.

28: - **Local Testing Principle**: Flashing hardware to test UI changes is slow and prone to dead-ends. Always build a decoupled, local-machine test harness (node servers, DOM mocks, Playwright) to iterate cleanly on HTML/JS before starting C++ integration.

1580: ### 16.2 `NATIVE_BUILD` Guard Pattern
1581: 
1582: All modules must compile on native (host CPU) for Tier 1 testing. The `NATIVE_BUILD`
1583: preprocessor define (set by `[env:native]`) controls hardware-specific code:
1584: 
1585: #### Architectural Rationale: The Cost vs Benefit of Native Builds
1586: 
1587: While littering the codebase with `#ifndef NATIVE_BUILD` guards may feel like a heavy aesthetic tax, it is the most important architectural discipline in the framework:
1588: 
1589: 1. **Iteration Speed:** Hardware-only testing (compile → flash via USB → boot) takes 15–45 seconds per cycle. Native GoogleTest execution runs in milliseconds, fundamentally changing how developers write and refactor logic.
1590: 2. **CI/CD Feasibility:** Native builds allow the full logic suite to run on standard cloud runners (e.g., GitHub Actions) without complex Hardware-in-the-Loop server farms.
1591: 3. **Forced Decoupling:** The host CPU lacks `<WiFi.h>` and `<LittleFS.h>`. This missing dependency actively prevents developers from tightly coupling high-level logic to low-level hardware drivers. It forces the use of forward declarations (e.g., `class U8G2;`) and dependency injection (e.g., passing `currentMillis` instead of calling `millis()`), ensuring business logic remains pure and testable.

1594: #ifndef NATIVE_BUILD
1595: #include <WiFi.h>
1596: #include <LittleFS.h>
1597: // ... hardware-specific implementation

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Host Testing Isolation & Compilation Portability**:
> Under the native build environment, standard hardware-dependent headers (such as `<WiFi.h>`, `<LittleFS.h>`, `<U8g2lib.h>`) do not exist. "Hello! During compilation of the native test suite, I identified 4 additional minor bugs that prevent native compilation:

1. **U8G2 Mock Missing Methods:**
   - **Issue:** The mock `U8G2` class inside `modules/u8g2Display/widgets/drawingPrimitives.hpp` is missing `drawPixel()`, `clearBuffer()`, and `sendBuffer()`.
   - **Fix:** Add empty inline stubs for these 3 methods inside the mock `U8G2` class.

2. **`getSystemMillis()` Redefinition Clashes:**
   - **Issue:** `getSystemMillis()` is defined individually as a `static inline` function inside `clockWidget.cpp`, `scrollingTextWidget.cpp`, `wifiStatusWidget.cpp`, and `u8g2DisplayModule.cpp`. Because `test_main.cpp` compiles by `#include`ing these `.cpp` files in a single translation unit, it causes redefinition errors.
   - **Fix:** Centralize `getSystemMillis()` inside the shared header `modules/u8g2Display/widgets/drawingPrimitives.hpp` and remove the redundant definitions from those 4 `.cpp` files.

3. **`SleepClockBoard` Missing Member:**
   - **Issue:** `SleepClockBoard.cpp` references a member variable `timeMgr`, but it is not declared in `SleepClockBoard.hpp`.
   - **Fix:** Declare `TimeManager* timeMgr;` as a private member in `SleepClockBoard.hpp` and forward-declare `class TimeManager;` at the top of the file.

4. **ArduinoJson Standard String Serialization Support:**
   - **Issue:** `u8g2DisplayModule.cpp` serializes directly to a `std::string` under native build, which fails because `ARDUINOJSON_ENABLE_STD_STRING=1` is not defined.
   - **Fix:** Add `-D ARDUINOJSON_ENABLE_STD_STRING=1` to the native environment build flags in `platformio.ini`.

Do I have permission to proceed with these edits?"

81: ## 3. Notable Design Implementations
82: 
83: ### OLED Burn-in Mitigation
84: The `SleepClockBoard` protects screens from pixel degradation by shifting its layout coordinates periodically:
85: *   A drift offset (`xOffset, yOffset`) is recalculated every 60 seconds.
86: *   Widget rendering is offset dynamically within a safe coordinates grid, keeping static items constantly in motion.
87: 
88: ### Power Management & Two-Stage Sleep
89: The `U8G2DisplayModule` acts as an idle state machine:
90: 1.  **First Stage (Screensaver)**: After `sleepTimeoutMs` (e.g. 10 minutes of inactivity), the display transitions to screensaver sleep by showing the floating `SleepClockBoard`.
91: 2.  **Second Stage (Power Off)**: If inactivity continues for an additional 10 minutes, the physical panel is completely powered down via `setPowerSave(1)` to conserve battery power.
92: 3.  **Wake Trigger**: Any user interaction (such as button clicks or active service overrides) wakes the module, restores power via `setPowerSave(0)`, and returns the screen to the active board carousel.

45: ## 3. Notable Design Implementations
46: 
47: ### Socket Protection via client-side FIFO Queue
48: To prevent ESP32 TCP socket exhaustion during rapid user navigation, all network requests are wrapped inside the `ApiQueue` class:
49: *   Calling `window.apiFetch(url, options)` queues requests.
50: *   Requests are resolved sequentially with a 50ms cooldown between active fetches, ensuring the ESP32 server recycles sockets gracefully.
51: 
52: ### Dynamic Routing Extension Loader
53: The portal is fully decoupled from third-party extension tabs:
54: *   On startup, the portal queries `/api/tabs`.
55: *   The response contains registered custom extensions (e.g. `[ { "name": "CustomTab", "endpoint": "/api/ext/custom/portal" } ]`).
56: *   The portal dynamically generates navigation buttons and, when clicked, fetches and mounts HTML content fragments inside `#dynamic-panels`.
57: 
58: ### Resource Compression
59: The static build script minifies HTML/CSS/JS variables and compresses the SPA bundle using `gzip`, reducing payload transfers from ~40KB to <12KB. Gzipped arrays are stored in Flash memory (`.rodata`) rather than dynamic heap allocations to keep memory usage minimal.
